jobs.title: Program Manager, Data Science Core & GenAI Studio
jobs.description:
**College Board - Technology - Data Science Core & GenAI Studio**

**Location:** This is a fully remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office).

**Type:** This is a full-time position

  

**About the Team**

The Data Science team develops analytical approaches, statistical models, and machine learning capabilities that help College Board make better decisions and deliver stronger outcomes for students and educators. Our growing team partners across research, product, engineering, business intelligence, and operations to turn complex questions and data into useful, responsible, and scalable solutions. This role supports both Data Science Core and Gen AI Studio teams.

  

The work spans exploratory analysis, experimentation, model development, production delivery, and ongoing monitoring. Accuracy, transparency, privacy, and responsible use of data are essential, particularly in high-stakes education contexts. What makes this team distinctive is its combination of rigorous data science, practical problem-solving, and sustained cross-functional collaboration.

  

**About the Opportunity**

As Program Manager, Data Science, you will create the structure and operating discipline that enables a growing data science portfolio to deliver meaningful results. You will connect strategy to execution by managing roadmaps, priorities, dependencies, risks, decision points, and communication across multiple workstreams. A core part of this work is making sure projects are ready before Data Science delivery begins: prerequisites confirmed, dependencies explicit, and decisions made on time.

  

You will partner closely with data scientists, data and software engineers, product managers, researchers, and business leaders. You will help teams translate ambiguous goals into executable plans, maintain momentum through changing conditions, and make tradeoffs visible. You are not expected to serve as the lead data scientist; you will bring enough technical fluency to understand the data science lifecycle, ask sharp questions, and help specialists do their best work.

Success in this role will be measured by the team's ability to focus on the highest-value work, deliver reliable outcomes predictably, manage risk early, and build trust with partners.

  

**In this role you will**

**Manage Delivery Risk and Program Operations (30%)**

* Establish lightweight, consistent operating rhythms for planning, status, decision-making, risk review, and retrospectives.
* Drive alignment across data science, engineering, and product stakeholders, ensuring dependencies and decisions are communicated clearly and on time.
* Identify delivery, data, model, compliance, and resourcing risks early; drive mitigation and escalate when timely decisions are needed.
* Track program health and outcomes using meaningful measures rather than activity alone, and use evidence to improve plans and processes.
Maintain clear program artifacts, including roadmaps, dependency maps, decision logs, risk registers, and executive-ready updates.  

**Orchestrate Cross Functional Execution (25%)**

* Coordinate work across data science, research, product, engineering, analytics, privacy, legal, security, and business teams.
* Build executable plans from ambiguous goals and align contributors on scope, responsibilities, milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
* Facilitate decisions and resolve blockers without replacing the judgment of technical or domain experts.
Manage handoffs from research and prototyping through production delivery, adoption, and operational ownership.  

  

**Drive Program Strategy and Portfolio Planning (20%)**

* Translate Data Science strategy and business priorities into a clear portfolio of programs, workstreams, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
* Own integrated roadmaps and planning processes, translating research priorities into sequenced milestones and tracking progress from experimentation through deployment.
* Lead intake and prioritization in partnership with Data Science leaders, balancing impact, effort, capacity, risk, and sequencing.
* Establish readiness criteria so projects have confirmed prerequisites, including data access, legal and privacy review, a named business owner, and agreed success measures, before Data Science delivery begins.
Define program success measures and establish clear ownership, decision rights, and escalation paths.  

  

**Build Stakeholder Alignment and Adoption (15%)**

* Serve as a trusted partner to technical and non-technical leaders, creating shared understanding of objectives, constraints, tradeoffs, and progress.
* Communicate complex data science work in clear language appropriate to the audience, including uncertainty, model limitations, and responsible-use considerations.
* Create feedback loops with users and stakeholders so that solutions address real needs and adoption is planned from the beginning.
Prepare concise recommendations and decision materials that help leaders act with the right context.  

  

**Strengthen Team Effectiveness and Scale (10%)**

* Partner with Data Science leadership on capacity planning, team growth, role clarity, and sustainable delivery practices.
* Protect focus by reducing avoidable interruptions, clarifying priorities, and improving how work enters and moves through the team.
* Promote documentation, reuse, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement across programs.
Support an inclusive, accountable environment in which people can raise risks, challenge assumptions, and learn from outcomes.  

  

**About you**

* You have 8 or more years of experience leading complex programs or portfolios in data science, analytics, machine learning, software, research, or another technical environment.
* You have a record of delivering cross-functional programs from initial problem framing through implementation, adoption, and measurement.

jobs.title: Senior Intelligence Analyst — National Security AI Evaluation (Remote)
jobs.description:
Senior Intelligence Analyst — National Security AI Evaluation (Remote) is a remote review track for evaluating AI outputs across senior intelligence analyst national security specialist operations workflows. Reviewers grade workflow correctness, policy adherence, and stakeholder fit; flag operational risk; and document the right next step so the modeling team can train on it.

**Why this role matters**
-------------------------

Senior Intelligence Analyst National Security specialist operations AI has to fit into an actual day at work. AuraOne uses experienced operators to grade outputs the way a senior peer would — checking workflow, policy, and the unwritten rules that decide whether a task actually gets done.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Review AI outputs against current senior intelligence analyst national security specialist operations workflows, playbooks, and firm policy for Senior Intelligence Analyst — National Security AI Evaluation (Remote) assignments.
* Grade tone, escalation logic, and stakeholder fit on a structured rubric.
* Flag operational risk, missed escalations, and policy-adherence gaps with severity tags.
* Capture the right next step so the modeling team can train on it.
* Adjudicate disputed treatments against published playbooks or firm guidance.
* Maintain reviewer-quality scores in inter-rater calibration cycles.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Direct working experience in senior intelligence analyst national security specialist operations on real teams for Senior Intelligence Analyst — National Security AI Evaluation (Remote) work.
* Comfort applying multi-page rubrics consistently across long batches.
* Clear written reasoning that names the policy or workflow being applied.
* Strong attention to detail and the ability to flag when a prompt itself is the problem.
* Reliable async availability for at least 10 hours per week.

**Example tasks**
-----------------

* Grade a model's response to a real senior intelligence analyst national security specialist operations ticket and rate workflow, tone, and escalation.
* Flag a missed escalation with the right severity tag and corrected next step.
* Adjudicate a disputed playbook call between two reviewers using firm guidance.
* Audit a 25-row batch for rubric consistency and report drift to the program lead.

**Nice to have**
----------------

* Prior experience training, calibrating, or QA-ing operations teams.
* Familiarity with AI-assisted workflow tooling and its failure modes.
* Bilingual experience for cross-region operations.

**Skills**
----------

* Operational review
* Policy adherence
* Workflow judgment
* Stakeholder communication
* Senior Intelligence Analyst National Security specialist operations

**Work model**
--------------

Remote — US-eligible. Remote · Independent specialist contractor. Employment type: CONTRACTOR. Applicants must be authorized to work from US.

**Compensation**
----------------

Hourly rate confirmed after the interview process.

**Application process**
-----------------------

Apply through AuraOne's specialist intake for role-specific routing and review. Final project scope, schedule, and contractor terms are confirmed before placement.

jobs.title: US Immigration Program Manager (Strategy & Operations)
jobs.description:
Meta is seeking an experienced U.S. Immigration Program Manager to drive the operating model and program direction for U.S. employment-based immigration, serving as a subject-matter expert on case filings and compliance operations. This role is accountable for filing quality, accuracy, and timeliness at scale, the program's U.S. compliance posture, and the frameworks, playbooks, and tooling that underpin delivery.This individual will partner closely with Recruiting, People Partners, Legal, external counsel, and business leaders to solve the most complex U.S. immigration challenges, ensure regulatory compliance, and continuously improve our case management operations. This is a senior individual contributor role operating with significant autonomy: identifying program priorities, resolving ambiguous cross-functional problems, and influencing decisions without direct authority.  
  
  

### **US Immigration Program Manager (Strategy & Operations) Responsibilities:**

* Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Meta's U.S. immigration operating model and compliance framework, including decision rights and controls for right-to-work verification, government reporting, audit readiness, and regulatory change management, in partnership with Legal, HR, and outside counsel
* Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on U.S. employment-based nonimmigrant and immigrant filings (e.g., H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN, PERM, EB-1/NIW/EB-2/EB-3, adjustment of status, and consular processing), partnering with Legal and outside counsel on case strategy, filing requirements, and adjudication trends
* Own program-level oversight of complex, high-profile, and time-sensitive immigration filings, personally leading selected escalations while scaling case preparation and execution through operational teams and outside counsel
* Develop and maintain standardized filing playbooks, templates, checklists, and quality-control protocols that enable consistent, high-quality case preparation at scale
* Monitor U.S. regulatory developments and proactively translate new requirements into updated policies, processes, and operational guidance with Legal and outside counsel
* coordinate with regional immigration leads where cases have cross-border dependencies
* Drive technology and process innovation in case management workflows: identifying opportunities for automation, AI-assisted checks with human review, and system enhancements to reduce cycle times and improve accuracy
* Act as an escalation point for complex filing scenarios, RFEs (Requests for Evidence), denials, and novel immigration questions, partnering with Legal and outside counsel on resolution paths and addressing systemic causes through process improvements
* Establish and enforce quality standards and SLAs for external immigration counsel and service providers, reviewing work product and driving accountability for filing accuracy and timeliness
* Partner cross-functionally with Legal, People Partners, Recruiting, and Finance to align U.S. immigration operations with workforce planning and talent strategy, resolve competing priorities, and clarify handoffs, with the PERM recruitment team owning recruitment execution and this role owning overall immigration case progression
* Develop compliance dashboards, reporting mechanisms, and audit processes that provide visibility into filing volumes, cycle times, compliance health, and risk exposure, and use these measures to prioritize improvements and hold teams and vendors accountable
* Set and drive a multi-quarter roadmap for the U.S. immigration program, identifying high-impact problems, making the case for investment, and sequencing initiatives against business priorities, risk, and delivery capacity with minimal management oversight

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of progressive experience in U.S. employment-based immigration with responsibility for case filings, compliance program design, and immigration operations, including end-to-end ownership of complex programs at scale
* Deep subject-matter expertise across U.S. employment-based nonimmigrant visa categories and permanent residence pathways, including PERM, immigrant petitions, adjustment of status, and consular processing
* Demonstrated experience designing and operating U.S. immigration compliance frameworks, setting program direction, and establishing decision rights and controls across teams and external providers
* Track record of developing scalable processes, playbooks, and quality frameworks that deliver measurable improvements across multiple teams
* Experience managing relationships with external law firms and immigration vendors, including setting quality expectations and enforcing SLAs
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders (Legal, HR, Recruiting, Finance), resolve competing priorities, and drive decisions in ambiguous situations without direct authority
* Experience leveraging AI or automation tools to drive efficiency in compliance monitoring and case processing workflows

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience operating within a global technology company or a similarly complex, high-volume immigration environment
* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
* Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
* Experience coordinating cross-border cases and partnering with regional immigration specialists outside the U.S
* Data-driven approach to measuring filing quality, cycle times, compliance health, and vendor effectiveness

From delivering affordable broadband to protecting against cybersecurity threats and building digital government services, OTI is at the forefront of how the city delivers for New Yorkers in the 21st century. Follow us on social media @NYCOfficeofTech, and visit www.nyc.gov/oti to learn more.
  
  
At OTI, we offer great benefits, and the chance to work on projects that have a meaningful impact on millions of people. You'll have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology and collaborate with other passionate professionals who share your drive and commitment to making a difference through technology.
  
  
About Cyber Command
  
Cyber Command is charged with protecting all City systems against cyber threats, including systems that deliver vital services to New Yorkers. Headed by the Chief Information Security Officer of the City of New York, we provide in-depth support to over 100 agencies and offices to protect, detect, identify, respond to, and recover from cyber threats.
  
  
Job Description
  
Cyber Command’s Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) program focuses on collecting, processing, analyzing, and disseminating actionable intelligence to stakeholders to provide the context needed to make informed decisions to respond to threats and mitigate risks to City systems and data.
  
  
The Cybersecurity Analyst (Cyber Threat Intel) within NYC Cyber Command perform many critical functions in support of the program’s areas of focus by providing direct support to executive and policy-focused stakeholders within Cyber Command and City agency leaders. The Threat Intelligence analyst will act as the liaison between the Cyber Risk team and the CTI team and providing intelligence in support of the Risk team’s Citywide risk assessment project by identifying and modeling the threats most relevant to the City agencies and digital services under assessment.
  
  
Responsibilities will include:
  

* Deliver strategic intelligence relevant to stakeholders within the City of New York in briefings and written reports
* Lead in the development of relevant, timely, and accurate threat intelligence support to leaders and Risk managers at NYC3: provide analyst support to NYC3 stakeholders and disseminate analysis through threat intelligence platform
* Enable the delivery of products and services in alignment with intelligence requirements: capture intelligence requirements and capture metrics on intelligence requirements serviced
* Support operation and improvement of the threat intelligence and analysis platform in coordination with the Content Manager and other analysts
* Engage in cross-team collaboration for Risk assessment workstreams
* Create and document detailed standard operating procedures and playbooks
* Support the intake and implementation of relevant feedback for intelligence products and services and map feedback to intelligence requirements (IRs)
* Contribute to the research and tracking of threat actors, malware, and campaigns: ensure that tracking is tied to intelligence requirements and coordinate with the CTI team and other teams within NYC3
* Maintain relationships with vendors that provide intelligence support, analytical support, and toolsets
* Handle special projects and initiatives as assigned.

Day - Due to the necessary technical duties of this position in a 24/7 operation, candidate may be required to work various shifts such as weekends and/or nights/evenings.

Brooklyn, NY

jobs.title: Fraud Strategy Analyst
jobs.description:
Identify emerging fraud and reduce chargeback losses across IDT and Boss Money products, including Mobile Wallet, Web, and WhatsApp. Use data and AI tools to investigate suspicious activity, evaluate automated decisions, and improve fraud controls.

### **Responsibilities:**

* Investigate suspicious activity across accounts, payment cards, devices, and recipients; identify linked behavior and patterns that individual transaction reviews may miss.
* Identify unusual transaction patterns, emerging fraud trends, and opportunities to detect suspicious activity earlier.
* Analyze fraud and chargeback activity across accounts, payment cards, devices, recipients, issuing banks, countries, and customer segments.
* Recommend new alerts, early-warning indicators, and monitoring reports that enable faster detection and response.
* Review fraud cases to understand what was missed and recommend improvements to existing controls.
* Work with fraud operations, rules, AI, and technology teams to implement and measure improvements.
* Identify potential fraud risks as Mobile Wallet, Web, and WhatsApp continue to grow.
* Present findings and recommendations to management in a clear, actionable manner.

### **Education Certification and Experience Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative, business, or related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Experience in fraud analysis, payment risk, or related investigations, including hands-on analysis of transaction data, is a plus.

### **Required skills:**

* Strong analytical and investigative skills, with a natural curiosity for identifying patterns and understanding why things happen.
* Ability to turn observations and data into practical recommendations.
* Comfortable using Excel, dashboards, and reports to analyze trends.
* Strong communication and problem-solving skills.
* Clear written and verbal communication; ability to document investigations, explain decisions, and collaborate with technical and operational teams.
* Familiarity with SQL, AI tools, or fraud detection systems is helpful but not required.

**About us:** IDT is a Communications and Money Transfer company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. IDT is an industry leader in prepaid communication, money transfer, and payment services, and one of the world's largest international voice carriers. We are listed on the NYSE, employ over 1800 people across 20+ countries, and have over $1.5 billion in revenues. Our flagship brand, Boss Revolution, offers Money Transfer, International Calling, and Mobile Top-Up services, supporting IDT's mission to enable people to stay connected and share resources with family and friends worldwide. **Join us!**

**Description**
---------------

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

**Northrop Grumman Corporate (NGCO)** is looking for a **Manager, Programs 3** to lead workstreams and develop processes, tools and other work products supporting the enterprise transformation of program management. This position will report to the Corporate Global Operations Program Management Excellence Director and support the team’s charter of advancing program management development, execution, and culture within Northrop Grumman.

This position is a full-time, hybrid role is based near a major Northrop

Grumman site, with the ability to travel as required (approximately 10%).

**What You’ll Get to Do:**

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager and Manufacturing Quality Engineer
jobs.description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. The people here at Apple don’t just create products - they create the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.  
  
In this highly visible role, you will have process (TPM) and quality engineering (MQE) responsibility for next generation Apple products. This will require you to lead selection, implementation & optimization of manufacturing processes and quality planning and deployment.  
  
In the TPM responsibility, you will utilize your Engineering experience and work cross functionally with Product Design Engineering and Industrial Design to assess product features for manufacturability, and recommend capable processes and equipment.  
  
In the MQE responsibility, you work in tandem with Apple's renowned designers to develop measurement & metrology technologies, quality control plans, information systems, and manufacturing methods that achieve industry-leading specifications at massive production scale. We handle a network of supplier factories worldwide, with responsibility for our partners to deliver to bold schedules. Our focus is on elegant execution of extraordinary industrial designs, resulting in products that thrill our customers.  
  
**Description**  
  
Process Development:  
  
Planning, proposing, and leading experiments to produce timely and accurate analyses used to drive design, development, and supply chain decisions.  
  
Assessing the suitability of a fabrication technology for a given part design. Planning validation exercises to demonstrate initial feasibility as well as manufacturing capability. Analyzing results of validation exercises and provide technical recommendations.  
  
Reviewing progress of development activities at supplier locations and serve as point of escalation for critical process related issues.  
  
New Product Introduction:  
  
Help to drive process development and capability assessment activities, reviewing part design documentation to ensure alignment with process capability.  
  
Assigns specific tasks and work with Apple suppliers to support process development and/or data gathering activities. Set clear goals for results and provide timely reviews of performance throughout program.  
  
Establish validation procedures to figure out acceptance of tooling into development builds as well as mass production.  
  
Supplier Execution:  
  
Review supplier tool design, process flow, equipment selection, DFM, and DOE proposals. Identify shortfalls and corrective actions to ensure design compliance.  
  
Work with supplier engineering teams to map out process development exercises, secure resources, and commit to schedules in line with program goals  
  
Assess supplier readiness to support build events and production ramp. Identify potential execution issues and provide recommendations to mitigate risk.  
  
You will utilize your Quality Engineering background in the following areas:  
  
Quality Planning  
  
Apply solid understanding of quality control and manufacturing concepts to develop specific Product Quality Plan (PQP) appropriate to program and commodity.  
  
Coordinate all Quality Engineering functions for a program, serving as project manager to lead efforts at supplier locations.  
  
Actively participate in the program planning and monitoring process assuming responsibility for key deliverables at all milestones.  
  
Provide technical direction and guidance to other Quality Engineers supporting the implementation of the PQP.  
  
Assess measurability and creatively address concerns directly with stakeholders. Identify and direct studies to implement improvements in measuring method where appropriate.  
  
Establish audit procedures appropriate to program and supplier to ensure adherence to Apple quality standards. Implement FAI and Cp/Cpk reviews of mechanical parts.  
  
Supplier Quality Management  
  
Assists supplier selection process for new products and second sourcing activities supporting qualification/disqualification decisions.  
  
Review PQP with supplier and other Apple functional groups to optimize supplier quality programs. Evaluates supplier readiness and adherence to PQP at all development and qualification stages.  
  
Monitor each supplier's performance through measurement of production line statistics, company inspections, and audits. Prepare summary of performance and communicate to appropriate management to ensure effective corrective action plans can be promptly executed.  
  
At Apple, a Supplier Quality Engineer defines product cosmetic specifications and manufacturing quality control methods. Reviews processing techniques and methods applied in the manufacture, fabrication, and evaluation of products. Involvement may begin at any step from product concept to full-scale manufacturing. Coordinates design requirement review with appropriate engineering/scientific personnel to ensure capability of manufacturing processes. Compiles and evaluates data to determine appropriate limits and variables for process, material, and part specifications. May conceive and plan projects involving definition and selection of new concepts, product inspection technology, and approaches in the processing or development of new or improved processes. Recommends and implements equipment and process modifications to improve production efficiencies, manufacturing techniques and production yields for existing products. Develops and conducts statistical analysis such as Design of Experiments (DOE) and Statistical Process Control (SPC) targe

Responsibilities include:

The Cyber Governance, Risk and Compliance Analyst will be tasked with continuously improving Cyber Command and will participate in Citywide cybersecurity risk assessments.
  
  
The Cyber Governance, Risk and Compliance Analyst will serve in a security risk, audit and compliance analyst role within the Cyber Command Audit and Compliance Division. The Analyst will help shape and assess NYC agencies' cybersecurity risks and compliance posture, enforce and ensure compliance with Citywide cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures and cybersecurity frameworks.
  
  
Responsibilities will include:
  

* Review security assessment and service performance reports to identify any significant issues or variances and initiate corrective actions where necessary.
* Review and analyze various cybersecurity risk cases, including justification and exceptions documents submitted by agencies.
* Assist in the development of cybersecurity risk and compliance assessment procedures and testing methodologies based on established frameworks and guidelines.
* Assess NYC Agencies’ documented information security and technology policies, procedures, and practices.
* Conduct evaluations of cybersecurity programs or their individual components to ensure compliance with Citywide cybersecurity policies and standards.
* Conduct risk-based cybersecurity audits of NYC agencies’ programs, projects, and initiatives, including evaluation of the design and operating effectiveness of security controls.
* Execute audit procedures, perform technical and procedural control testing, evaluate supporting evidence, and document results in accordance with established audit methodologies.
* Draft and present finding reports accompanied with working papers, concise controls assessments, and systems testing reports (both narrative and table based).
* Prepare and maintain audit working papers that support observations, findings, conclusions, and recommendations; communicate audit results clearly to stakeholders.
* Track and validate remediation of audit findings, cybersecurity control deficiencies, and compliance gaps.
* Analyze legal, regulatory, contractual, and policy requirements relevant to cybersecurity controls and compliance; support clear documentation of compliance gaps and related recommendations.
* Engage in communications with NYC Agencies to assist Agencies in complying with Citywide policies and standards, and
* Handle special projects and initiatives as assigned.
